B.3 WOODY BIOMASS | FT | RD In this process, woody biomass (50% clean pine, 50% forest residue blend) is dried and sent to an indirectly heated gasifier followed by tar reformer (Tan et al., 2015) to generate syngas. Then syngas is sent to the gas cleanup unit to remove ash, CO and adjust H to CO ratio in the syngas 2 2 to about 2:1 for downstream synthesis. The clean syngas is sent to a fixed bed Fischer-Tropsch (FT) reactor filled with cobalt-based catalyst. The FT reactor products include light gases and FT liquid, which are separated via a series of flash tanks. The FT liquid is then upgraded in hydrotreating and/or hydrocracking unit to produce gasoline and diesel-range fuel blendstocks. B.4 SEWAGE SLUDGE | HTL | BIOCRUDE In this process, the slurry sludge is converted into biocrude at a non-catalytic reactor operated under subcritical water status (20 MPa, 350°C), while aqueous-phase product, gas, and solid are generated as byproducts. The HTL reactor products are separated via filter, flash tank, and decanter. The HTL aqueous phase product has higher ammonia and chemical oxygen demand (COD), a measure of the amount of oxygen required to chemically oxidize organic compounds in B-1 a water sample, than wastewater stream being treated in a conventional wastewater treatment facility. Several technologies such as ammonia stripping and wet air oxidization, can be used to reduce ammonia and COD of HTL aqueous phase product before recycling it back to the wastewater treatment facility. Biocrude intermediate can be considered as a fuel blend or further upgraded to diesel and aviation fuels via hydroprocessing and fractionation. B.5 WOODY BIOMASS | CFP (PT/TIO ) | BIO-OIL 2 Ex-situ catalytic fast pyrolysis (CFP) technology using a Pt/TiO catalyst is selected to represent 2 the most recent state of technology for CFP-based renewable diesel. In this process, biomass from a feedstock handling unit is sent to a fast pyrolysis reactor with heat supplied by hot sand. The solid phase product contains mainly ash, char, and sand, which is sent to the char combustor. From there, hot sand is circled back to the pyrolysis reactor to heat the endothermic reaction. The vapor- phase product is sent to the ex-situ catalytic vapor upgrading reactors. The upgraded pyrolysis vapor is sent to the CFP product condensation unit to be separated into organic liquid CFP bio-oil and aqueous wastewater stream. Valuable oxygenated coproducts are generated with additional recovery and purification equipment.
